page: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor. The configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor is equipped with 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 4.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per core. Storage is bundled with a 30 GB local SSD, and the server includes 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs.

Benchmark results show strong single-core capabilities but moderate multi-core and memory performance. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rank in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU scores fall into the average tier. Memory bandwidth is average, with read-only large block speeds at 68.79 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 50.39 GB/sec. Notably, PassMark memory scores and database operations are weak, ranking in the bottom 25%.

This server offers high single-threaded performance relative to its entry-level hardware class, making it a cost-efficient option for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core utilization. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can introduce performance variability under heavy neighbor load, alongside the weak database and memory performance indicated by PassMark benchmarks.

The STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic static web serving, and simple background tasks. It is also appropriate for small-scale development environments, basic Redis caching, and low-demand utility services that fit within the 4.0 GB memory and 30 GB SSD storage limits.
description: UpCloud STARTER-2xCPU-4GB is an entry-level virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with x86_64 architecture. It features 2 shared vCPUs, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 30 GB of local SSD storage, with no GPU. Performance benchmarks reveal a stark contrast: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded gzip compression rank in the top 10%, whereas multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain average. Crucially, database operations and PassMark memory scores fall into the bottom 25%, highlighting a performance bottleneck for memory-intensive tasks. Given its shared CPU allocation and qualitative cost efficiency, this server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, static web serving, and basic development environments rather than heavy database or multi-threaded production applications.
